### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. stiff skin syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.791)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:3603)

**Proposed mechanism:** FBN1 (HGNC:3603) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormality of the skeletal system (HP:0000776); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormality of the skin (HP:0000951). Mutations in FBN1 disrupt extracellular matrix organization, leading to both skeletal abnormalities (MONDO:0013612) and skin abnormalities (MONDO:0008492).

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in FBN1 that are exclusively associated with one disease and not the other, or if the functional consequence of FBN1 variants differs significantly between the two diseases (e.g., LoF for one and GoF for the other). _(variant: rs746905567)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular basis in FBN1 can facilitate the development of targeted therapies that address the common downstream pathways, potentially benefiting patients with either disease.

#### 2. Weill-Marchesani syndrome 2, dominant  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.782)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:3603)

**Proposed mechanism:** FBN1 (HGNC:3603) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal connective tissue development (HP:0003198); FBN1 (HGNC:3603) —LEADS_TO→ Ectopia lentis (HP:0001075); FBN1 (HGNC:3603) —LEADS_TO→ Tall stature (HP:0004301); FBN1 (HGNC:3603) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004322); FBN1 (HGNC:3603) —LEADS_TO→ Joint hypermobility (HP:0001382); FBN1 (HGNC:3603) —LEADS_TO→ Megalocornea (HP:0000517); FBN1 (HGNC:3603) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital glaucoma (HP:0000610); FBN1 (HGNC:3603) —LEADS_TO→ Short, broad hands and feet (HP:0001190); FBN1 (HGNC:3603) —LEADS_TO→ Brachydactyly (HP:0001178); FBN1 (HGNC:3603) —LEADS_TO→ Cutis laxa (HP:0001069); FBN1 (HGNC:3603) —LEADS_TO→ Contractures (HP:0002790). Heterozygous variants in FBN1 lead to haploinsufficiency, resulting in defects in fibrillin-1 deposition and microfibril assembly. This disrupts connective tissue integrity and affects various organ systems, manifesting differently in MONDO:0013612 (e.g., tall stature, joint hypermobility, ectopia lentis) and MONDO:0012013 (Weill-Marchesani syndrome 2, dominant; e.g., short stature, brachydactyly, glaucoma, megalocornea, contractures, cutis laxa), reflecting differential effects on connective tissue components and developmental pathways.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct causal genes for each disease in independent cohorts, or demonstration of completely opposing functional consequences (e.g., gain-of-function for one and loss-of-function for the other) of FBN1 variants in each disease. _(variant: Presence of common pathogenic variants in FBN1 (e.g., allele frequency >0.1% in gnomAD) that are associated with both phenotypes would weaken the hypothesis of these being rare disease-specific mutations.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in FBN1 allows for the exploration of common therapeutic strategies targeting extracellular matrix integrity or specific downstream signaling pathways affected by fibrillin-1 dysfunction. Differential phenotypic outcomes highlight the complexity of genotype-phenotype correlations and the need for personalized treatment approaches.

#### 3. MASS syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.781)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:3603)

**Proposed mechanism:** FBN1 (HGNC:3603) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0007047); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0007047) —LEADS_TO→ Aortic aneurysm (HP:0002670); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0007047) —LEADS_TO→ Scoliosis (HP:0002670). Mutations in FBN1 lead to disruption of extracellular matrix organization, resulting in phenotypes such as aortic aneurysm (characteristic of MASS syndrome) and scoliosis (a shared phenotype).

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of pathogenic variants in FBN1 with loss-of-function effects in patients with MONDO:0013612 and gain-of-function effects in patients with MASS syndrome, or vice versa, would falsify this hypothesis of shared haploinsufficiency. Additionally, the identification of distinct causal genes for each disease that do not converge on FBN1 function would falsify this shared causal gene hypothesis. _(variant: Pathogenic variants in FBN1 with allele frequencies > 0.01 in gnomAD exomes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving FBN1 haploinsufficiency provides a unified therapeutic target for both MONDO:0013612 and MASS syndrome. Therapies aimed at restoring FBN1 function or mitigating the downstream effects on extracellular matrix integrity could benefit patients with either condition.

Mutations in FBN1 lead to haploinsufficiency, disrupting the organization and biogenesis of the extracellular matrix, which in turn results in the phenotypic manifestations of Marfan syndrome (including aortic root aneurysm) and isolated ectopia lentis.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in FBN1 with loss-of-function effects in patients with Marfan syndrome (MONDO:0013612) and pathogenic variants with haploinsufficiency effects in patients with isolated ectopia lentis (MONDO:0007514) would support this hypothesis. Conversely, if the primary mechanism for one disease involved gain-of-function mutations in FBN1 while the other required loss-of-function, this shared mechanism would be falsified. _(variant: The presence of common variants in FBN1 (e.g., allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD) that are not associated with either disease would suggest that the disease-causing variants are rare and specific.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in FBN1 for both Marfan syndrome and isolated ectopia lentis can inform diagnostic strategies and potentially lead to targeted therapeutic interventions aimed at restoring fibrillin-1 function or mitigating downstream consequences of its deficiency.

**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1474228, Reactome:R-HSA-216083)

**Proposed mechanism:** FBN1 (HGNC:3015) —DISRUPTS→ connective tissue development (GO:0007101); connective tissue development (GO:0007101) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal connective tissue morphology (HP:0003198); HSPG2 (HGNC:4931) —DISRUPTS→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0002650); connective tissue development (GO:0007101) —BINDS→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198).
